title: Subword Tokenization — BPE, WordPiece, Unigram, SentencePiece

questions.question: What does word_counts do with uppercase words in the corpus?
options: It lowercases them before counting
It drops them because the pattern accepts only lowercase input
It keeps a separate count for every capitalization
It turns each uppercase letter into a boundary token
questions.explanation: The regex accepts letters and the code applies text.lower() before constructing the Counter.

questions.question: What is the initial symbol sequence for "low" from init_vocab?
options: ("l", "o", "w") without an end marker
questions.explanation: BPE starts with characters and appends </w> so word-final merges remain distinguishable.

questions.question: How are pair counts weighted when "low" occurs five times?
options: Each pair contributes one regardless of word frequency
Only the final pair receives the word frequency
Every adjacent pair from low contributes five to its count
The word is ignored until it appears ten times
questions.explanation: pair_counts adds freq for every adjacent symbol pair in each vocabulary entry.

questions.question: What does merge_pair do when it finds the selected pair twice in a row?
options: It merges only the final occurrence
It recursively merges every possible overlapping substring
It deletes both symbols instead of creating a token
It merges each non-overlapping occurrence from left to right
questions.explanation: The while loop appends the combined symbol and advances by two whenever the pair matches.

questions.question: Why does train_bpe stop early when pair_counts returns no pairs?
options: There is no adjacent symbol left to merge
The requested number of merges was automatically doubled
The corpus has been translated into another language
All tokens have become unknown and must be discarded
questions.explanation: The loop breaks when the pair Counter is empty; otherwise it selects the most frequent pair and continues.

questions.question: What does encode_bpe("slowest", merges) preserve even if the word was unseen during training?
options: A guaranteed single whole-word token
Character-level pieces, plus </w>, replayed through the learned merges
A lookup from the training corpus that must contain slowest
Only the first character, because unseen words are rejected
questions.explanation: Encoding starts from the word characters and applies known merges, so unseen words can still decompose into pieces.
